psychnets: Psychometric Network Estimation

Source: R/psychnets-package.R
psychnets-package.Rd

psychnets estimates psychometric networks and assesses their accuracy, stability and differences. A psychometric network represents psychological variables, such as items, symptoms or behaviours, as nodes and their associations as edges; it shows which variables are directly related, which are central, and how the structure differs between groups.

The cross-sectional estimators are reached through psychnet() or called directly: Gaussian graphical models (ebic_glasso(), ggm_modselect(), huge_network()), information-filtering networks (tmfg_network(), logo_network()), relative-importance networks (relimp_network()), correlation and partial-correlation networks (cor_network(), pcor_network()), Ising models for binary data (ising_fit(), ising_sampler()) and mixed graphical models (mgm_fit()). Panel data from a few waves are modelled with the panel graphical VAR (panel_gvar()). Fitted networks are read with as.data.frame(), net_centralities(), net_predict() and certificate(); their accuracy, stability and group differences are assessed with net_boot(), net_stability() and net_compare().

Certificates

Each regularized or constrained estimator stores how far its network is from satisfying the optimality conditions of its objective, so that the fitted network can be checked without a second solver. certificate() reports this value for any fitted network.
